the proposed CNN-based method is able to solve ill-posed inverse problem with a high accuracy, a high efficiency, and a high robustness, compared with the traditional methods.
the proposed network can be used to replace the iterative reconstruction in X-ray CT, and can achieve comparable or even better performance than iterative reconstruction.
we have proposed a novel deep learning framework to solve inverse problems in imaging, and we have demonstrated its efficacy in sparse-view X-ray CT reconstruction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep learning can be used to solve inverse problems by combining direct inversion with a CNN that learns to remove the artifacts introduced by the direct inversion.
deep CNNs can be used to solve normal- convolutional inverse problems, even if the forward operator is non-differentiable.

the structure of iterative algorithms for solving ill-possed inverse problems is similar to that of deep CNNs and that the CNN structure can therefore be leveraged to solve such problems in a data-driven manner, without the need for explicit regularization.
